facts.text: Founded in 1732 by Jean‑Pierre Roma, Three Rivers is one of Prince Edward Island’s earliest French settlements.
The town sits where the Cardigan, Brudenell, and Montague/Valleyfield rivers meet, creating a harbor that opened the province’s interior.
During the age of sail, Three Rivers thrived as a shipbuilding center, producing vessels and serving as a busy port from 1840 to 1889.
The Three Rivers area hosts seven of Prince Edward Island’s 30 drowned forest sites, showcasing its post‑glacial geological history.
East Isle Shipyard in Georgetown continues the town’s shipbuilding legacy by constructing tugboats for the modern maritime industry.
In 2004, the Cardigan, Brudenell, and Montague/Valleyfield Rivers were collectively named a Canadian Heritage River for their cultural and recreational value.
